Chromium Visible Engine DaisyUI 5 Cyberdeck Bézier Kinematics Multi-Tab Capable LanceDB Cortex Memory MCP Standard Compliant

Mark Eleven is an interactive, stateful web-browsing Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that empowers multimodal LLM Agents (such as Bonsai 2 27B, Gemini, Claude, and GPT-4o) to operate the live, open web like a human operator inside a real, visible Chromium browser instance.

🌌 Neuromancer Inspiration & Cyberpunk Canon

"A Kuang Grade Mark Eleven penetration program. Icebreaker. The military stuff, the heavy artillery."
— William Gibson, Neuromancer (1984)

In William Gibson's seminal cyberpunk masterpiece Neuromancer, console cowboys Case and the ROM personality construct of the Dixie Flatline jack into the Matrix using an Ono-Sendai Cyberspace 7 cyberdeck. Their ultimate weapon: the Kuang Grade Mark Eleven—a legendary military-grade icebreaker designed to slice through corporate ICE.

Kuang Grade Mark Eleven channels this lineage: piercing modern anti-bot heuristics (Cloudflare, CAPTCHAs, SPAs) with an authentic visible Chromium chassis, organic cubic Bézier pointer movement, and persistent LanceDB memory recall.

🎯 Core Architecture Principles

  1. 100% Real Browser Chassis: No headless emulation, synthetic user-agent spoofing, or sandboxed scraping. Mark Eleven runs a full-fledged, visible Chromium instance (headless: false) with hardware acceleration, audio/video capabilities, and authentic cookie/session persistence.
  2. Multimodal Vision Integration: Specifically tailored for multimodal models. The agent takes high-res viewport screenshots (take_screenshot) to visually understand layouts, buttons, and dynamic canvas states, and can act directly by coordinate, selector, or mark badge (act).
  3. Full Developer Console & Script Execution: Gives the agent full console access (get_console_logs) to inspect runtime errors and API output, plus arbitrary JavaScript evaluation (evaluate_javascript) to interact with complex SPAs.
  4. Behavioral Bot Detection Bypass: Bypasses Cloudflare, Akamai, Datadome, and behavioral bot sensors by avoiding synthetic element.click() events (isTrusted: false). Instead, it dispatches real input over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (Input.dispatchMouseEvent / Input.dispatchKeyEvent / mouseWheel) accompanied by organic cubic Bézier pointer movement and human Gaussian typing cadence. CDP delivery is focus-independent — it lands even when another app owns the OS foreground — with webContents.sendInputEvent kept only as a fallback.

📑 Multi-Tab Browsing Engine

Mark Eleven supports tabbed browsing powered by Electron's modern WebContentsView pool with zero-flicker bounds swapping:

  • Autonomous Popup Trapping: External links with target="_blank" or window.open automatically spawn a new tab pill in your Cyberdeck without opening native external OS windows.
  • Memory Isolation: Each tab maintains its own isolated DOM tree and JavaScript context while sharing the stealth TLS session.
  • DaisyUI Tab Bar: Dynamic status dots (loading vs active), title truncation, close buttons, and + new tab creation.

🕹️ Ghost Cursor Telemetry Engine

  • Organic Bézier Trajectories: Natural cubic Bézier curve calculation with quintic ease-in/ease-out acceleration, micro-jitter, and target deceleration.
  • Focus-Independent CDP Delivery: Input events are dispatched over the tab's attached CDP debugger (Input.dispatchMouseEvent / Input.dispatchKeyEvent / mouseWheel) with focus emulation enabled, so clicks, keystrokes, and momentum wheel scrolling land regardless of which window owns the OS foreground. webContents.sendInputEvent remains only as a fallback; bridge_health reports input.transport (cdp | native).
  • Occlusion-Proof Rendering: Browsing tabs run with backgroundThrottling: false plus the Chromium switches --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows, --disable-renderer-backgrounding, and --disable-background-timer-throttling, so an occluded window still hydrates and fires scroll events — lazy-load harvests keep working behind your editor.
  • Anti-Bot Defense Bypass: Satisfies enterprise heuristic sensors (Akamai, Cloudflare) by behaving like a genuine physical operator.

🔌 Standardized Semantic MCP Tools (62 advertised · +2 optional)

62 advertised tools (82 registered entries; 23 deprecated aliases stay callable by name but are hidden from tools/list), plus two optional tools — drive and decide — shown shaded above and listed first when a decision model is configured (see the Decision Layer section below). Seven OKF resources are also exposed: (mark-eleven://skills/guide, mark-eleven://tools/recommended, mark-eleven://okf/manifest, and four partition playbooks).

Start here. Read with observe, interact with act, wait with wait_for, locate with find, and pull structured data with extract / collect_all. Reach for take_screenshot (TIER 2) or evaluate_javascript (TIER 3) only as fallbacks.

The table below groups the tools you will reach for most by tier; the complete advertised set (with full parameter schemas) is available at runtime via help() and tools/list.

act mark_id?: number, selector?: string, x?: number, y?: number, action?: 'click' | 'focus' | 'hover' | 'type' | 'press', text?: string, secret?: boolean, clear_first?: boolean, await_conditions?: object[], timeout_ms?: number, dry_run?: boolean The interaction entry point: one humanlike action addressed by mark ref, CSS selector, or coordinates, with optional post-conditions and a delta report. 🎥 Timelapse Recorder

The HUD can record itself as a timelapse — useful for showing how an agent worked, or for attaching a short clip to a form that asks for a video. The REC button sits next to SETTINGS; the recorder's options live in Settings → Recording.

A frame is captured every interval (default 1000 ms) and played back at the chosen frame rate (default 30 fps). One minute of real work therefore becomes about two seconds of video. The file is VP9 in a WebM container, so it plays in browsers and uploads without transcoding.

  • Enable the recorder — turns the REC button and the recording tools on or off.
  • Output directory — where finished files are written. The default is the app's recordings/ folder; BROWSE… picks another directory.
  • Capture every / Playback fps / Max width / Bitrate — trade file size against smoothness. Lower the interval for busy interfaces; raise it for long sessions.
  • Recent timelapses — every file with COPY PATH, so a path can be pasted straight into a file-upload field.

Agents can do the same with record_start, record_stop and list_recordings. record_stop returns the absolute path; that path is an ordinary string, so it can be typed into an upload field that accepts a value, or handed to a human when the field only opens a native file picker.

⚙️ Optional Decision Layer — decide & drive

Kuang works without it. When a decision model is configured — Settings → Decision model in the HUD, or KUANG_DECISION_* environment variables, or data/decision.json — two extra tools are advertised first in tools/list. With none configured they are absent entirely, so nothing offers a tool that would only answer NOT_CONFIGURED.

The split: Jev picks which component and what operation; the agent supplies text; Kuang executes and verifies every action. The model never writes prose, never becomes a selector, and is never called behind your back.

decide — one typed decision

Send a state plus typed questions (choice / score / noul) and get the answers back verbatim, with probabilities and confidence. TypeSafe's choice takes criteria (option → description), not options — the wrong shape comes back as a misleading 422.

Guard + elimination: pass guard to reject low confidence, targets that were not offered, targets that cannot perform the operation, and done/blocked answers that also name a target. eliminate removes a rejected option and asks again (max 5); when nothing survives the call returns accepted:false, fallback:"agent" and no action is taken.

Human hand-offs: age-verification and CAPTCHA copy is detected before any model call. decide returns 409 HUMAN_REQUIRED, spends no model call, and raises the HIL request itself. A model-only blocked with no matching copy is handed to the agent to decide. Enabled gate calls can attach a viewport screenshot — hosted TypeSafe only; the OpenCode gateway does not forward the required header, so images are disabled there and the result says so.

drive — the loop, in code

drive({ goal, values }) repeats observe → guarded decide → verified act until the goal is met or it must stop: done, blocked, human_required, needs_agent, failed, max_steps. It never invents text: a typing step without a supplied value returns needs_input naming the field, and you call again with it. dry_run plans the first step without acting.

Measured on four page scenarios: Jev 1.13 10/10 at ~376 ms; local kev-0.6b 7/10 at ~830 ms; open-jev 6/10 at ~1.25 s. The local path is labelled experimental for that reason. Full design notes, the runner-side example (scripts/drive-example.mjs) and the update/signing plan: docs/DECISION_MODELS.md and docs/BUILDING.md.
